name: Costco

header.one_liner: The most loyal customers in retail and steady 6% to 7% comps, at 46 times earnings.
header.thesis: Costco grew fiscal 2026 net sales 10% and EPS 14% to $20.76, with comparable sales up 6.6% excluding gasoline and currency, a 92.3% renewal rate in the US and Canada, and digital sales up a fifth. Nothing in the business is wrong. At about 46x fiscal 2027 earnings, the share price already assumes it stays that way for a long time.

base.eps_label: FY2027E diluted EPS (year to August 2027): fiscal 2026 $20.76 less the $0.15 tariff-refund benefit, grown about 10%
base.rev_label: FY2027E total revenue ($B): fiscal 2026 $303.2B grown about 8.5% (comps, about 25 net new warehouses a year, membership fees)

rev_cagr.why: Comparable sales grew 6.6% in fiscal 2026 excluding gasoline and currency, on a 5% higher average ticket and 3% more shopping trips, plus 25 net new warehouses. The base case holds about 7.5% a year.

margin_end.why: Net margin is about 3.0%: Costco deliberately keeps merchandise margins thin and earns on membership fees ($5.9B, +11%). The base case adds a little margin from membership fee growth and Kirkland Signature mix.

share_chg.why: Costco bought back only about $0.85B of stock in fiscal 2026 against a market value above $450B; it prefers special dividends.

exit_pe.why: Today's multiple is about 46x fiscal 2027 EPS, near the top of Costco's range and above Walmart. The base case assumes it drifts toward 40x as EPS grows about 10% a year.
exit_pe.source: Engine judgment; current multiple computed from price and FY27E EPS

pillars.title: Comparable sales are steady
pillars.claim: Fiscal 2026 comparable sales grew 6.6% excluding gasoline and currency: 5% from ticket, 3% from traffic.

evidence.t: Net sales $297.2B, +10.1%; total comparable sales +8.4% reported, +6.6% adjusted

pillars.title: Members keep renewing
pillars.claim: Paid members reached 84.1M, Executive members 42.3M, and renewal rates were 92.3% in the US and Canada.

evidence.t: Membership fee revenue $5,907M, +11%; worldwide renewal rate 89.8%

pillars.test: Does the worldwide renewal rate stay near 90% as international members grow?

pillars.title: Digital is growing fast
pillars.claim: Digitally-enabled comparable sales grew 20.7% in fiscal 2026, excluding gasoline and currency.
pillars.test: Does digital growth come without diluting gross margin?

pillars.title: Thin margin by design
pillars.claim: Gross margin fell 3 basis points (up 10 excluding gasoline); Costco reinvests to keep its pricing authority.

evidence.t: Q4 EPS $6.75 included a $0.15 benefit from tariff refunds, partly reinvested in member values

pillars.test: Does EPS growth stay near 10% without one-offs?

variant.street: The market pays about 46x fiscal 2027 earnings for the most consistent retailer in the world.
variant.ours: The business is close to flawless; the multiple is the risk. Our base case grows EPS about 10% a year and lets the multiple drift toward 40x, which earns less than the cost of equity over 12 months.
variant.could_be_wrong: If the market keeps paying any price for consistency, the multiple holds and returns track EPS growth plus the dividend.
variant.would_change_mind: The price nearer 38x earnings, or another membership fee increase that lifts EPS growth into the mid-teens.

review.basis: Fiscal 2026 10-K (year to 30 August 2026) and Q4 release. Q1 fiscal 2027 reports in December; this review refreshes after the print.
review.headline: Close to a flawless retailer. At 46x earnings the stock is priced like one.
review.model: Costco charges an annual membership fee for access to warehouses that sell a limited range of goods at very low markups. Membership fees are most of the profit; merchandise is sold close to cost to keep members loyal.

how_it_earns.v: $5.9B a year from 84M paid members; most of operating profit.
The largest category: groceries, snacks, household goods.
Electronics, home, apparel; meat, produce and bakery.
Gasoline, pharmacy, optical, food court: traffic drivers at thin margins.

mix.note: Reported geographic segments for fiscal 2026. Operating margin is segment operating income over total revenue including membership fees.

rows.label: Other international
rows.driver: Mexico, Japan, UK, Korea, Australia, Taiwan, China and Europe

review.position: The largest warehouse club in the world and one of the largest retailers, competing with Walmart's Sam's Club and BJ's.

sources: Buying scale on a limited assortment
moat.threat: The valuation, not competitors: no rival has matched its renewal rates.

Digitally-enabled comps +20.7% excluding gasoline and currency.

facts: 25 net new warehouses in fiscal 2026; 939 in total

flags.flag: Valuation risk acknowledged by the company

forecast_basis.exit_pe: Judgment: drift down from near the top of the range

base.story: Comps 6% to 7%, 25 to 30 new warehouses a year, EPS about 10%; the multiple drifts toward 40x.

downside.story: Comps slow to the low single digits and the market stops paying for consistency; the multiple falls toward 32x.

upside.story: A membership fee increase and a special dividend lift returns while the multiple holds.
upside.needs: Fee increase in the next two years

risks.how: At 46x earnings, a move to Walmart-like or historical multiples would cost far more than a year of EPS growth.
Ticket growth includes inflation; slower inflation or weaker consumers would slow comps.
Digital-first members renew at lower rates than long-time warehouse shoppers.
Gasoline prices swing reported sales and margins; tariffs raise costs on imported goods.
Fee increases have come about every five to seven years; the last took effect in September 2024, so fee growth slows until the next one.

peer_read.why_premium: Costco has the highest renewal rates and most consistent comps in retail, and net cash.
peer_read.why_not: Walmart now trades near 41x with faster digital and advertising growth; BJ's trades at about 22x.
peer_read.peers_note: Target and Dollar General trade at much lower multiples on weaker sales trends.

questions: What multiple is right for 10% EPS growth, however reliable?
When is the next membership fee increase?
Can digital keep growing 20% without diluting margins?

arguments.label: Growth
arguments.text: Fiscal 2026 net sales grew 10% with comparable sales up 6.6% excluding gasoline and currency, and digitally-enabled sales up about 21%.

arguments.label: Moat
arguments.text: 84M paid members renewing at 92% in the US and Canada, buying scale on a limited range, and Kirkland Signature. No rival has matched it.

arguments.label: Profitability
arguments.text: A 3% net margin by design: merchandise is sold close to cost and $5.9B of membership fees (+11%) make most of the profit.

arguments.label: Capital
arguments.text: Net cash of about $15B funds about 25 new warehouses a year, a $5.88 dividend and occasional special dividends.

arguments.label: Valuation
arguments.text: {peer_line} About 46x earnings is near the top of Costco's own range.

thesis_long: Costco is the most consistent large retailer in the world. Fiscal 2026 sales grew 10%, comparable sales grew 6.6% excluding gasoline and currency on both higher tickets and more trips, digital sales grew about a fifth and the renewal rate in the US and Canada held at 92.3%. EPS rose 14% to $20.76.

The problem is only price. At about 46x fiscal 2027 earnings, the stock trades near the top of its range and above Walmart, and the company's own 10-K warns that the share price reflects high expectations. EPS growth near 10% a year cannot keep up with even a modest return toward historical multiples.

Our base case grows EPS about 10% a year and lets the multiple drift toward 40x, which earns less than the cost of equity over 12 months. We would turn positive nearer 38x earnings, or on a membership fee increase that lifts EPS growth into the mid-teens.

upside_risks.how: A fee increase drops almost entirely to profit and would lift EPS growth for two years.
Costco has paid large special dividends from excess cash; another would add several points to the return.
